audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven full-layer chart rows read "Skill" while the content layer and the packet both read "Fizz".
audit.why: 55.21% over 1065 games; packet levelChart is Fizz on all seven, and content win[0..6] is Fizz on all seven. The full layer's phases[].side said Skill on all seven, so the page rendered two different answers to every stage. The whys already describe Fizz winning each stage, which confirms Fizz is the intended verdict.
audit.corrected: All seven full-layer sides set to Fizz; ratings on rows 0-3 raised from 5/10 to 6/10 to match. No why needed rewriting for the verdict since each already described Fizz winning.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike framing was fine; the ultimate cooldown was never given.
audit.why: Fizz spikes at 3 (Playful/Trickster), 6 (Chum the Waters), first item. Neeko's counter-spike is Pop Blossom at 120/105/90s — a 600-range leap with a knockup and stun whose preparation is hidden while she is disguised.
audit.corrected: Pop Blossom's 120s/90s cooldown written into breakdown.cooldowns; breakdown.spikes left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told the reader to sidestep Tangle-Barbs "behind minions", which is the opposite of what the ability does, and never mentioned that Fizz grounds Pop Blossom.
audit.why: Riot's Tangle-Barbs text: it roots everything it passes through, and if it kills an enemy or passes through a champion it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer. Standing behind the wave feeds it a minion kill and makes the root bigger. Separately, Pop Blossom carries the dash flag and both Playful/Trickster and Chum the Waters carry grounding, which is the missingInteractions entry for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Rewrote dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, tldr and loading around lateral sidestepping; wrote the grounding interaction into breakdown.mid and dontsFull[0].d.

audit.why: Tangle-Barbs 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and Pop Blossom 120/105/90s are both in the kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] and the content 'late' paragraph both call the root "Blooming Burst" (packet suspectNames flagged this).
audit.why: Blooming Burst is Neeko's Q, a seed that deals magic damage and blooms again — it has no root. The root is Tangle-Barbs (E).

notes:
CHART: all seven full-layer sides read "Skill" against "Fizz" in both the content layer and the packet — a seven-for-seven cross-layer disagreement. Every side edit here moves the FULL layer onto the value win[N] already holds on disk, so no content win[N] edit is proposed (the target string is already there and a no-op edit would be rejected). Post-apply the layers agree on all seven rows, and each why already described Fizz winning that stage.

BIGGEST FIX: the page repeatedly advised sidestepping Tangle-Barbs 'behind minions'. Riot's text says the tangle grows larger, faster and roots longer if it kills an enemy or passes through a champion — hiding behind the wave feeds it. That advice was actively harmful and is now inverted.

NAME ERROR CONFIRMED: the packet's suspectNames hit is real. wants.foe[0] and the content 'late' paragraph both attributed the root to Blooming Burst (Q); the root is Tangle-Barbs (E). Both corrected.
